seo.name: Matheapolis
seo._name: The wordmark on its own, for og:site_name (src/layouts/Layout.astro). The club was the Minneapolis Math Book Club until 2026-11-07, when the operator rebranded it: "I want the focus on the people and the ideas more than the book. the book is more an inspiration". A site_name that carries a descriptor makes two claims in the field a platform uses to label its source, so the descriptor lives in "title" instead. Do not use this slot to rename the Meetup group or the Mobilizon group - those are other organisations' records, listed in design/grill/copy-options.mjs as ORG_OF_RECORD.
seo.title: Matheapolis - a Minneapolis math club
seo._title: Was 'Join the Minneapolis Math Book Club | Math Book Discussions' — an imperative and a keyword phrase, in the voice of a listing rather than the club. og:title and twitter:title read this slot, and it is what a search result bolds, so it is the wordmark plus the descriptor. The descriptor names Minneapolis, from two rulings on 2026-11-08: first that it must print the city the wordmark puns on rather than say “Twin Cities” (the club's name is a play on `Math` inside `Minneapolis`), then that naming Minneapolis alone is sufficient here (operator: “Remove St. Paul from the subtitle of the club name. Minneapolis being named is sufficient for the subtitle and SEO”). It is the same phrase the hero's label lane carries, with the article kept because a title is read as a sentence fragment and the lane is a label. `scripts/check-copy.mjs` asserts the two slots stay coupled: three files hold this phrase, and a copy edit that reaches two of three is this repo's documented defect class. Google documents no length limit on a title link — it truncates to fit the device — so nothing here is tuned to a character count @retrieved 2026-11-08 from developers.google.com/search/docs/appearance/title-link. Both forms were measured in the lane's own face and case: 257px of ink with the article, 243.7px without, in a 288px lane at 320, one line box either way @measured 2026-11-08 by `npm run round16`. The 2026-11-07 ruling this slot carried (“A Twin Cities math club”) is recorded in `src/components/HeroSection.astro` and D240. It does NOT carry the old name: the continuity line is in the hero copy, where a person reads it, and the old apex keeps serving rather than 404ing, which is what actually preserves six years of links (D112's locator rule, applied to metadata). The share card is not a slot for this ruling — its kicker already prints “Minneapolis, MN” (scripts/make-social-share.mjs).
seo.description: A Minneapolis math club. We work through papers, proofs, proof assistants and puzzles together, around a table in a coffee shop or a brewery. Dates on Meetup, a sign-up link on every date, and the discussion in the chat.
seo._description: Was 'Connect with fellow math lovers in our vibrant reading community. Monthly meetups, engaging discussions, and diverse book selections in Minneapolis, MN.' — 'vibrant', 'engaging' and 'diverse' are unsourced adjectives, and 'diverse book selections' describes a service the club does not run (2026-11-03). No cadence word here: the one cadence claim the site makes is the hero label, and it carries its source in src/content.json (D92). This sentence is also what a link unfurl shows, so it is written for a person. Re-read it when the venues or the paths change; `check:content` scans <meta content> for cadence words, so adding one means adding a source. 2026-11-08, twice: “in the Twin Cities” became “in Minneapolis and St. Paul”, then the same-day correction named Minneapolis only. “in Minneapolis coffee shops and breweries” is the shortest form that still backs itself up: the venues the page sources are in src/content.json (`venues`, and the `venueCount` line says the club has used fifteen places around the Twin Cities), so the metro claim stays on the page in body copy while the metadata names the city the wordmark puns on. Google documents no length limit on a meta description either — it truncates to fit the device @retrieved 2026-11-08 from developers.google.com/search/docs/appearance/snippet — so this is written for a person, and `check:content` still scans it for cadence words that would need a named source. 2026-11-11 (D273): the sign-up clause moved from naming Meetup to naming the schedule - 'a sign-up link on every date' - because `src/lib/rsvp.mjs` now decides per date which platform holds the sign-up page, so naming one platform in the metadata is a claim the page no longer makes.

URLs._rule: Every non-empty URL here is printed on a page as a promise about a site this club does not control, so each one carries a dated verification stamp in `_verified` (S019, D272). `npm run check:rsvp:links` re-measures them with one GET each and writes the stamp; `npm run check:rsvp` fails the build when a configured link has no stamp, a stamp older than 60 days, a URL that is not the shape its platform can have (`LINK_SHAPES` in src/lib/rsvp.mjs), or a stamp that last answered 4xx/5xx. One key is an exception, and the exception lives in code, not prose: `facebookGroup` is in `PROBE_BLIND_KEYS` because every anonymous request this rig can make to facebook.com answers 400 whatever the URL is - a group that exists and an id that cannot exist both answer 400 @measured 2026-11-11 by `node scripts/check-rsvp.mjs --links` (Linux native, browser UA, redirects followed) - so a status code there is not evidence. For that key the gate asks the network nothing and asks a human something: the URL must match the group shape and carry `confirmedBy` and a `confirmedAt` inside the same 60-day window (S021, D280). A 2xx/3xx from any future probe still counts as the strongest evidence and makes the confirmation unnecessary. A platform whose entry is empty is not rendered: src/components/SignUpLinks.astro takes its destinations from signUpPaths() in src/lib/rsvp.mjs, and scripts/check-rsvp-page.mjs asserts the absence from the built bytes rather than trusting the component's silence. All four keys must be present, empty or not - an unchosen platform is not the same thing as a closed one.

_verified._how: One anonymous GET each with a browser UA, redirects followed, from the dev rig (Linux, native - no WSL, no Docker). Written by `npm run check:rsvp:links`. The 60-day limit is LINK_STAMP_DAYS in src/lib/rsvp.mjs, the same age rule check:figures applies to a measured number in DESIGN.md (D151).

facebookGroup._note: The status in this stamp proves nothing about the URL: measured 2026-11-11 (Linux native, curl, browser UA, redirects followed, one request each) facebook.com answers 400 to /groups/matheapolis, /groups/MinneapolisMathBookClub, /matheapolis, /pg/matheapolis and /groups/zzzznotarealgroup1234567890 - an id that cannot exist - identically @measured 2026-11-11 by the same anonymous GET this probe uses. So the evidence for this link is the operator's word, recorded in .notes/SESSIONS.md: the group is public at https://www.facebook.com/groups/matheapolis (S021, D280). Re-confirm within 60 days, or run `npm run check:rsvp:links` again and let a 2xx/3xx replace the confirmation.
